scope: Native ARPL compiler APIs, DS-safe lowering and actual NeverD HighC/LLVMC source interoperation

contract.source: Clang and Linux i386 NeverC provide arpl_reg, arpl_mem and arpl_mem_address32 builtins. Register form returns the adjusted word and stores native ZF after the call; memory forms own the m16 read/conditional write and return ZF.
contract.lowering: Ordinary pointers use a DS-preserving register class excluding BP/SP. Explicit offsets carry constant 16/32-bit address width and a validated segment prefix. Long mode and invalid controls are rejected. Calls keep unknown memory effects and cannot be speculated or removed for unused results.
contract.neverd: One X86SystemStateNative inventory feeds LLVM and both C writers. ARPL native selection requires the address32 capability, which identifies DS-safe lowering. Header-free builtin dispatch and exact assembly fallback work with both full LLVM and r6. C headers are requested only by the shared owner for APIs that need declarations.

qualification.counts: Native matrix: direct LLVM and Clang code16/code32 plus NeverC code32, O0/O2 on both cores. Each recovered-source run independently compiles 48 C exports and wraps eight ELF objects at O0/O2. 24 source images cover ELF/COFF/MachO, both NeverD optimization settings and register/DS/FS/GS operands. Non-ELF source is recompiled for SysV32; COFF/MachO objects are not executed.
qualification.negative_controls: Wrong source before intact ARPL and inverted ZF after intact ARPL are rejected. Returned-ZF corruption is rejected independently at O0/O2 for each actual-source compiler/SDK run.

diagnosed_failures: Old native pointer lowering could select BP/SP and silently choose SS. Shared DS-safe address lowering plus a BP-producer regression fixes it.
HighC requested immintrin.h for an ARPL helper that needs no declaration. A shared header-selection owner fixes the real NeverC i386 compile failure.
The KVM fixture incorrectly required the called ARPL PC to follow the wrapper entry. It now bounds both independently within the image; initial failures are retained under attempt1-*.
limits: Native code16 retains a 32-bit stack/pointer compiler ABI; NeverC source qualification is Linux code32 only.
NeverC embedded i386 machine selection and runtime remain unavailable; full LLVM performs object generation.
This proves instruction-boundary state and ABI-compatible compiled returns. It does not supply original-image fault dispatch or general i386 state reconstruction.
Real/VM86, asynchronous events, external devices and the other global SMM/SGX/transaction/state qualification boundaries remain separate.
reproduction: NeverC: tests/neverc/X86/verify_protected_arpl.py --llvm-bin LLVM_BIN --mode 16|32 --output OUT [--frontend CLANG_OR_NEVERC]; pin CPU affinity with taskset.
NeverC: tests/neverc/X86/verify_arpl_source.py --exports EXPORTS --output OUT --llvm-bin LLVM_BIN --frontend COMPILER [--fallback for stock Clang].
